sources.entry: Learn Vim For the Last Time: A Tutorial and Primer

summary.title: Learn Vim For the Last Time
summary.one_liner: Vim is taught as a language of verbs, modifiers and nouns, so the commands become a system you can reason about rather than a list to memorize.
takeaways: Vim commands combine a verb (d, c, y, v), an optional modifier (i, a, t, f, number) and a noun (w, s, p, b, t) into sentence-like commands.
Normal, Insert, Visual and Ex modes are introduced through the transition from Normal to Insert mode.
Basic .vimrc tweaks suggested include mapping jk to Esc and changing the leader key to a key on the home row.
The dot command repeats the last change, and combining a search (n) with . speeds up repeated edits.
summary.summary: This 2011 tutorial by Daniel Miessler teaches Vim as a language rather than a list of commands, arranged in sections for basics, getting stuff done, advanced use and quick tricks. It covers a suggested .vimrc setup (jk for Esc, a leader key, search and line-number options), plugin loading through the pack directory, and the verb-modifier-noun model. It then walks through movement, search, modes, insert, delete, yank and paste, spellcheck, substitution, buffers, windows and tabs, and the dot command with text objects. The page is partway through text objects when the captured text ends.
